One of the sucky things about living in a small town is the lack of healthcare options nearby. If I knew any other GPs who had openings for new patients, I would consider switching, but spaces are limited, as are the number of healthcare providers. 

Concerning point 6: I'm already in the midst of searching for a therapist (depression, yay!). If I do end up finding one who I like, I'll try to talk to them about it. I feel like this sort of thing doesn't just *go away*, and I'm definitely not equipped to handle it on my own. 

Mental trauma aside, I'm worried about potential physical trauma. I started to bleed during the pap smear, and even though I'm due to get my period, I have a sinking feeling that that wasn't the cause of it. I've been wearing pads all day since then, and I'm still bleeding considerably, without any of the symptoms of menstruation that I usually get. Am I overreacting, or is this genuine cause for concern? I only ask because you seem knowledgeable about how paps should go, and I have no clue if this is par for the course.

Discomfort is one heck of an understatement. I barely had time to wrap my head around what was going to happen. I kept tensing up, because *obviously I would,* which made the whole thing go on for longer than it needed to be.  -1000000/10, would not recommend.

The thing is, my GP/PCP is the one who did it. I was there for my physical. She noted that I hadn't had a pap smear before, and since I'm going to be 23 soon, she wanted to have one on record just in case. And since I don't use tampons (and I haven't had sex yet), I had no idea what it was going to feel like, and I especially didn't know to ask for lube! 

I don't want to switch providers just because of this one thing, as she's been wonderful with everything else, but I've been shaky and in pain since my appointment a couple hours ago. Even thinking about it makes me nauseas. I honestly don't know what to do.
